commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: refactor(outbound): move the bench breakdown into the To-ship find field
commits.body:
The per-bench ORDER counts shipped as a full-width chip row inside the KPI
band. That is the wrong home twice over: it spent a whole band of vertical
height on the densest desk in the app, and a facet that narrows ROWS belongs
beside the query that narrows them (house law 2026-08-08, enforced by
band3-find-only.guard.test.ts) — the Band-3 right zone is view toggles only.

It is deliberately NOT inside the Views menu. Views is a saved-snapshot
store (`saved_views` / useSavedViews); a facet is not a saved view. The
relationship already runs the other way and works: `packStation` is one of
To-ship's saved-view `paramKeys`, so a view REMEMBERS the bench rather than
hosting the control.

- `BenchRefineFacet` mounts in the find field's `trailingSuffix` as a
  `WorkbenchFilterPopover density="field"`, listing every bench with its
  count (empty benches included — "Station 3 · 0" is a real answer) plus
  Any bench / At a bench. Counts come from the queue-counts payload the KPI
  band already reads, so it costs no extra fetch. Pre-pack lanes only.
- `togglePackStation` / `togglePackPlaced` / `clearPackPlacement` join
  `useToShipFilterActions` — the surface's ONE URL write path. That is what
  keeps `?packStation=` and `?packPlaced=` mutually exclusive; a second
  writer is exactly how those two would drift apart.
- The aggregate "At stations" KPI tile stays. It is an attention metric,
  not a facet, and it is the at-a-glance number.

E2E rewritten for the new home (the old test asserted the deleted strip).

NOT RUN: Playwright is unusable in this tree — a concurrent session is
mid-upgrade (package.json + pnpm-lock modified; node_modules at 1.60.0
against a 1.58.2 pin), which breaks `test.skip()` at file scope in specs I
never touched. tsc, knip and 42 Band-3 / saved-views guards are green.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: feat(orders): show the packing bench as an opt-in Station column on To-ship
commits.body:
"Which bench is this order at?" belongs on the row, as a status chip — and
most of it already existed. `pack_location_id` / `_name` / `_kind` are
selected on EVERY orders row by `/api/orders`, and a `packStation` column
already shipped on the Tested lane. Two things were wrong with it:

- The fields were undeclared on `ShippedOrder`, so both consumers cast the
  row inline. That is how a field already on the wire stayed invisible to
  the type and to the default lane.
- The cell hand-rolled `.replace(/^QA\s+/i, '')` instead of the label SoT,
  so it drifted from the bench chips showing the same benches elsewhere.

Now:
- `ShippedOrder` declares the three fields; the grid cell drops its cast.
  (`UnshippedTable` keeps a wider row cast for other undeclared fields.)
- To-ship gets `packStation` as `tier: 'optional'` + `hideKey` — in the
  canonical column ORDER but OFF by default, opted in from the ▦ column
  display. Unbox History treats Serial / Vendor exactly this way, so the
  default lane is unchanged for anyone who never opts in. Verified live:
  the default header set has no `packStation`; enabling the staff delta
  adds the track.
- The cell renders through `GridStatusCellValue` — the same primitive as
  the Receiving status column — with the label from `packBenchShortLabel`
  and one shared tone (`PACK_BENCH_CHIP_TONE`, bg+text only since the cell
  supplies its own ring). Unstaged rows fall back to the quiet em dash,
  which the primitive already does, so the cell needs no branch.
- No dot: staging vs desk is carried by the label, and a dot would be a
  second channel for a fact the word already gives.

E2E asserts the column is absent by default, appears once opted in, and
paints a bench chip for a staged order.

commits.subject: refactor(orders): retire the To-ship column-header fork onto the shared factory
commits.body:
`OrdersQueueColumnHeader` was a 358-line fork of `LedgerGridColumnHeader`.
It was allowlisted when the factory genuinely could not do the job — no
resize grips, no width clamps. The factory grew both, and by the time this
was measured the fork was re-implementing it line for line:

  ORDERS_QUEUE_RESIZABLE_KEYS === ORDERS_QUEUE_COLUMNS.filter(isGridColumnResizable)
  ordersQueueHeaderShowsLabel === gridHeaderShowsLabel   (the fn GridHeaderLabel calls)

Half of it was unreachable: the `gridSkin={false}` branch carried a whole
second "board / Packed" header look (centered labels, canvas/95 backdrop
blur, inset:'cell'), and the single live mount always passed `gridSkin`.

Orders now composes `makeLedgerGridColumnHeader` like every sibling family,
so To-ship and Unbox History — the table SoT — share one header. Orders
*gains* the Sheets column context menu it never had, and header tooltips
that name it.

`selectMode: 'always'` preserves behaviour exactly: the fork resolved
`selectMode || gridSkin` with gridSkin always true, so select-all was armed
unconditionally — which is also the documented To-ship contract.

- Drops the now-orphaned ORDERS_QUEUE_COL_HEADER_STICKY (dead board branch).
- Amends the resize guard to pin the CONTRACT (one shared header, hence one
  shared handle) rather than the fork's direct import, which would now fail
  for a surface that became more shared, not less.
- source-of-truth.md: the "permanent allowlisted fork" row is retired.

all six columns in order with the frozen pane and no console errors.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(right-rail): render a picked occupant once, not twice
commits.body:
RightRailHost derived push-vs-overlay from `frame.mode`, which lags the
occupant's push demand by one render (the demand is published in an effect,
after commit). So a push occupant like Unbox History's `detail:history`
inspector mounted in the OVERLAY branch first, then swapped to PUSH once the
frame store round-tripped — and AnimatePresence keeps the losing overlay
`motion.aside` alive through its exit. Under throttled rAF that exit never
completes, so one carton rendered TWO panels with TWO live "Delete carton"
controls.

Decide push/overlay synchronously from the occupant's own `wantsPush` intent
(the host already computes it) instead of the lagging `frame.mode`. A push
occupant now only ever mounts in the push branch — no overlay→push handoff,
no duplicate. The frame store still owns `capPx`; only the mode decision moved
local. Reordered so `wantsPush` (and its `collapsed` dependency) computes
before `isPush`; the parked-no-strip latch is preserved.

Tighten the History delete spec to assert exactly one panel (toHaveCount(1))
in place of the `.first()` workaround. Verified on the QA org (qa-desktop).

The handoff explained HOW but never WHY, which is the part that decides
whether the next session judges this worth continuing. Five reasons, in
plain language, with the counter-argument stated rather than hidden:

1. A dead export looks like a supported API — it is a wrong turn left on
   the map, and "compose from the named SoT" only works if the named
   thing is the real one.

5. It is the only cleanup that is provably safe — zero callers means
   tsc + tests prove it in minutes, unlike the DS ratchets' 1,677 real
   call-site migrations.

makes it harder to pick up later, which is why the classification has
three buckets and why §6 (parked) exists at all.

commits.subject: refactor(nav): a page's "modes" are CHILD PAGES — spine vocabulary + label pass
commits.body:
Phase B of the spine work. The answer was already in the code: every child
carries `to(): { pathname, params }` and every parent a `resolveChild(location)`,
and the two round-trip — so they are distinct, deep-linkable, reload-safe URLs.
`nav-destinations.ts` said it outright ("/products?view=qc is a place, not a
setting"); the flatten made it structural, since a child is now an ordinary
spine row beside its parent. "Mode" named a drill that no longer exists.

B1 — renamed across 22 nav files, compiler-guarded one symbol at a time:
  SidebarModeItem      → SidebarChildPage       .modes        → .children
  resolveMode          → resolveChild           modeId        → childId
  filterPageModes      → filterPageChildren     applyModeTarget → applyChildTarget
  resolveSidebarMode   → resolveSidebarChild    useRecentModes  → useRecentPages
  useSidebarModeNav    → useSidebarChildNav     useActiveSidebarMode → useActiveSidebarChild
  HeaderModeSwitcher   → HeaderPageSwitcher     MODE_ICON_GLYPH_KEYS → STATION_GLYPH_KEYS
  RECEIVING/TECH/SHIPPING_MODE_ICONS → *_NAV_ICONS

The wire is UNTOUCHED and must stay so: `?mode=` is bookmarked
(/dashboard?mode=sales, /support?mode=voicemail, /review?mode=catalog-link) and
`getSidebarNavPageId` parses it. Proven, not eyeballed — all 74 param
expressions byte-identical to HEAD. The `sidebar.recentModes` localStorage key
is deliberately kept for the same reason; renaming it would silently empty every
operator's recents.

Two names deliberately NOT changed: `PACKING_MODE_ICONS` (packing styles —
standard/fragile/multi — are a genuine mode vocabulary, not child pages, and
/pack declares no children), and SettingsSidebarPanel's page-local resolveMode.

The §2 fork settled as KEEP, on a measured fact rather than taste:
ResponsiveLayout holds `navOpen` in an unpersisted useState(false) — the spine
is closed on every cold load (sidebar-open-close.spec.ts asserts it). Deleting
the header control would leave a bench operator with no visible way to switch a
page's children. The master-detail law now bans a twin RAIL rather than
asserting the spine cannot reach a child, which the flatten retired.

B2 — 8 of 10 labels. The three-way `Labels` collision is gone:
  Catalog › Labels    → SKU Barcodes      Fulfillment › Labels → Postage
  Locations › Labels  → Bin Tags          Catalog link         → Listing match
  Fulfillment › Orders → To ship          Support › Orders     → Inquiries
  Analytics Monitor   → Live Ops          Fulfillment          → Outbound
"To ship", not the brief's "Queue" — Sourcing already owns a Queue, which is
exactly why an overloaded word cannot identify one list. Zero ids, hrefs or
permissions moved: 180/180 literals identical to HEAD.

  · Local Pickup → Will Call — resolves no collision, and the nav is 1 of 7

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: feat(debt): repo-native dead-surface probe — what has nobody used?
commits.body:
The one standard that could not be built from what was already here. `knip`
answers "is this code reachable from an entry point"; it cannot answer "does a
human ever do this" — which is precisely how chrome Fields and the grid lip both
stayed "used" for months while only one of them was ever opened.

`npm run debt:surfaces` reads the typed action vocabularies out of the code
(`AUDIT_ACTION`, `InventoryEventType`, `ACTIVITY_MAP`) and asks the database
which of them have written no rows in 90 days. A code the product DECLARES but
the data has never SEEN is a surface with no users.

Chosen over an APM deliberately. Sentry/Datadog/PostHog give real statement
coverage, but cost a bill plus a client bundle this repo actively polices
(`build-gotchas.md` → bundle altitude); Vercel-native is request-level and would
not have caught the Fields fork, since both doors were live routes. This is the
~80% answer at ~0% cost and it composes the SoT the app already writes.

**REPORT ONLY.** Never a gate, never in `verify`, always exits 0 on a finding —
it reads production-shaped data, and a warehouse's quiet quarter must not be
able to fail a build. It also finds dead SURFACES, not dead BRANCHES: rows prove
someone reached the surface, never that every path inside it runs. Both caveats
print with the output, because a report that gets read as coverage is worse than
no report.

First run on the dogfood tenant: 170 silent codes (audit 157/236, inventory
12/19, station 1/9) — a worklist, not a verdict. Rare-but-critical paths
(revoke, recovery, conflict branches) are supposed to be quiet.

It also reports the OTHER drift direction, which was not asked for and turned
out to matter: 26 codes exist in the database that no SoT declares. The
vocabulary is incomplete, and an undeclared code is invisible to every consumer
that switches on the registry.

`occurred_at`, not `created_at`, on `inventory_events` — that table records when
the thing happened, and a backfilled row's insert time would claim a surface was
used the day we migrated it.

commits.subject: fix(debt): the ledger must never report zero because it could not read
commits.body:
`ratchets()` asked `git ls-files` and swallowed the failure, returning `[]`.
Anywhere git cannot answer — a `git archive` export, a CI cache, a tarball —
the ledger printed "DS ratchets 0 across 0" and read as a codebase carrying no
DS debt at all.

That is the exact false-clean signal this script was written to remove, so it
is a worse bug here than it would be anywhere else: a ledger that reports zero
when it cannot read is worse than no ledger. Caught by running it inside a
pristine `git archive` copy of HEAD while verifying attribution.

Walks `src/` directly now — the filesystem is the thing being measured — and
exits non-zero if `src/` itself is missing rather than reporting a total it did
not compute.

predicates. What it had no answer for is *when a flag stops*.

That gap is not cosmetic. A flag keeps BOTH branches reachable, so every
dead-code tool sees two live paths for as long as the flag exists — a permanent
strangler is a fork that has been made invisible on purpose, which is the same
blind spot as a two-door fork wearing a config file. Several flags here are
explicitly mid-migration (`isUnifiedEngine*`, the four `isPlacementStrangle*`,
`surface_composed_render`), and `backend-patterns.md` called the unified-engine
path "mid-strangler, so it is not yet a hard requirement". A strangler with no
deadline is how the losing branch becomes zombie code.

`FLAG_LIFECYCLE` now gives each flag `env`, `bornAt`, `area`, and a disposition:
`permanent` (with a reason), `rollout` (with a date), or `undecided`.
`feature-flags.guard.test.ts` fails on an overdue `undecided` (90 days), a
lapsed `plannedRemoval`, a flag with no entry, or an entry with no flag — that
last one being the direction that rots silently.

Two things deliberately not done:

**No vendor.** LaunchDarkly would be a second flag system beside the SoT module.
One file, one guard, no dependency, no dashboard.

**No invented dates.** Every `bornAt` is the first commit that introduced the
predicate, read out of git history. 26 flags land as `undecided`, which is the
honest state — fabricating removal dates nobody committed to would recreate the
unfalsifiable prose this guard exists to replace. The oldest flag is ~74 days
against a 90-day limit, so this lands green and starts biting in the ordinary
course rather than failing a build on arrival.

The registry lives in a dependency-free sibling and is re-exported: importing
`feature-flags.ts` pulls `@/lib/db` and its `server-only`, which threw the
moment the guard imported it. `build-gotchas.md` → bundle altitude, applied.

`backend-patterns.md` corrected: it documented the two private helpers as the
API, which is not what anything imports.

`knip-baseline.json` (2,888 parked findings) plus every `const *_BASELINE = N`

commits.subject: docs(rules): a retirement is not done until the old path is deleted or guarded
commits.body:
Institutionalises the lesson from the two retirements that quietly rotted this
week, and closes the live instance.

**The rule** (`pattern-evolution.md` → Always #6): a retirement is not done until
the old path is DELETED, or a guard names the exact surviving call sites,
shrink-only. A prose-only retirement is a TODO wearing a ruling's clothes.

The reason it has to be a law rather than advice is that a rules file cannot
fail. `source-of-truth.md` said `useIsColumnHidden()` "survives only for
`ChipColumns` / `RowMetaColumns`" while FOUR surfaces called it;
`workbench-ops-queue.md` described chrome Fields as the live entry long after 11
of 13 grids had moved to the lip. Both sentences were true when written and
stopped being true in silence.

Recorded alongside it: `knip` cannot see a fork whose doors are both imported.
It answers "is this reachable", never "is this the only way in" — which is why
the Fields fork survived months of clean dead-code runs.

**The instance.** `use-is-column-hidden.guard.test.ts` pins the real four —
`ChipColumns`, `RowMetaColumns`, `OrderIdentityChips` (chip/meta SLOTS that
paint inside a cell the row already owns, so there is no track to remove) and
the pre-LedgerGrid `StationRowColumnHeader`. It fails in both directions: a new
consumer, and a stale allowlist line left behind by a finished migration. Both
were exercised before landing.

It counts CALLS, not mentions — the grid families reference the hook in
docblocks to explain why they no longer use it, parens included, so the guard
strips comments first. A guard that flags its own explanation teaches people to
delete the explanation.

Both SoT rows now say four and name them.

Two shapes of the same defect: a symbol reachable by more than one name, which
is what let the retired-Fields fork hide from `knip` (both doors were imported,
so both were "used").

**Redundant default exports (12).** Each of these modules exported one symbol
both named and default, and nothing anywhere default-imported them. The named
export stays; `export default` goes. None is a Next.js page, where a default
export is the framework contract.

**The hooks barrel.** `src/hooks/index.ts` re-exported ~27 domain hooks and 29
types with **zero** barrel consumers, while the same hooks were imported by

now matches the code, and the barrel keeps only the `_*` category hooks plus
the four domain hooks that genuinely have barrel consumers.

reachable from an entry point, so file-level dead-code detection could never

at all. Deleted here: 638 LOC that `knip` reported as zero orphaned files. A
barrel that re-exports something nothing imports doesn't just widen the public

commits.body:
Empty marker commit — no tree change. It exists because the work described
below was committed under another session's message by accident, and the
history cannot be corrected: 6581c6211 is already pushed to origin/main, and
rewriting it would need a force-push (blocked by .claude/settings.json, and
wrong regardless for published history).

WHAT HAPPENED
Between `git add` and `git commit`, a concurrent session committed 6581c6211
and swept 18 staged files into it. The follow-up commit captured only a stray
staged deletion and was undone with `reset --soft`. The code landed correctly;
only the attribution is wrong. This commit is the record.

WHERE IT LIVES
All of it is in 6581c6211. Verified by diffstat that each file below contains
only these changes:

  src/app/api/auth/staff-picker/route.ts          24+/1-
  src/app/api/auth/workspace/route.ts             21+/2-
  src/app/api/entity-signals/route.ts             13+/3-
  src/app/api/orders/queue-counts/route.ts        11+/1-
  src/app/api/assignments/route.ts                 4+/1-
  src/app/api/silent-empty-response.guard.test.ts (new)
  src/components/auth/StaffPickerList.tsx         51+/7-
  src/lib/migrations/column-reference.guard.test.ts        (new)
  src/lib/migrations/migration-slot-uniqueness.guard.test.ts (new)
  src/lib/work-orders/fetch-all-queues.ts         39+/4-
  src/lib/my-day/aggregate-my-day.ts              17+/12-
  src/lib/tenancy/qa-org.ts                       65+/0-
  scripts/provision-qa-org.ts                     83+/6-
  scripts/run-pending-migrations.mjs              50+/6-
  tests/e2e/my-day-today.spec.ts                 108+/106-
  .claude/rules/backend-patterns.md               32+/0-
  docs/todo/daily-triage-FRONTEND-PLAN-VALIDATION.md 3+/0-
  docs/agent-log/entries/main.md                  (1 of 4 added lines)

1. HONEST FAILURE AT THE API LAYER
A caught throw must not be indistinguishable from "nothing exists". Of 38 catch
blocks returning 2xx, five answered an unexpected throw with a silent empty
collection. /api/auth/staff-picker (PRIMARY — no salvageable half, since PIN
sign-in is impossible without the roster) now answers 503 with degraded+error;
StaffPickerList gained its own retryable state, because the status alone was not
enough: the client had `if (r.ok)` and left staff:[] on every failure, so it
still rendered "No active staff" — the lie lived on both sides. /api/auth/workspace
is PARTIAL and keeps 200 (platformProviders is env-derived and still works during
a DB outage) plus degraded. entity-signals, orders/queue-counts and assignments
are SUB-RESOURCES: 2xx + degraded. Each states its failure class in its docblock.
Guard armed at 0, shrink-only, escape `api-allow-silent-empty` for webhooks that
must ACK.

2. EXPAND -> CODE -> CONTRACT
column-reference.guard.test.ts resolves qualified alias.column and bare columns
in single-table SELECTs against migrations + Drizzle. Verified it reproduces BOTH
2026-08-01 incidents: simulating an absent avatar_photo_id flags staff-picker
plus four more sites. Tuned for precision over recall via a resolver-confidence
rule; allowlists frozen, shrink-only, keyed on names rather than file:line.
Fixing its `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN a, ADD COLUMN b` parse (only the first was
read) recovered four real columns. migration-slot-uniqueness.guard.test.ts
freezes the 25 historical YYYY-MM-DD<letter> collisions. The runner gained
--only <file>, which refuses to skip an earlier pending file. Rule written up in
.claude/rules/backend-patterns.md.

3. QA FIXTURE DEPTH — THE BFF STUB IS GONE
provision-qa-org seeds three TEST work_assignments (one per due horizon, deadline
at 20:00Z so the civil-day bucket cannot flip with DST) plus an undated support
follow-up. doNext is DERIVED, never seeded: equal status and priority make
compareWorkOrderRows break the tie on deadline, so the overdue row is both doNext
and assigned[0] — reproducing the pointer relationship the duplicate-row bug
lived in, against real data. New test asserts the do-next row renders exactly
once, with a precondition that doNext.id really is inside assigned so it cannot
pass for the wrong reason. 12/12 green, three consecutive runs.

4. GET /api/my-day: 3,507ms -> 1,877ms (-46%)
The handoff prescribed pushing the "mine" predicate into SQL. Measurement says
otherwise: cost is per-QUERY round-trip, near-independent of rows — sku-stock
takes 736ms to return ONE row, listTechQueueItemsForStaff ~1.0s to return ZERO.
Narrowing result sets buys almost nothing. What cost the 1.6s was three serial
waves where nothing reads another's result; collapsed into one Promise.all, plus
a concurrent fan-out in fetchAllWorkOrderQueues that skips the flag read when the
caller passes `unified`. MyDayFeed's shape is unchanged.

REPORTED, NOT REPAIRED (other lanes' committed work)
- 2026-07-29f's _contract half is named .sql though its docblock calls itself
  .sql.gated, and sorts BEFORE its _expand half; both already applied.
- orders.serial_number / orders.tested_by in tech-logs/search look like rot given
  remove_tester_id_from_orders.sql.

KNOWN GATE GAP, DOCUMENTED IN THE GUARD
A RENAMED-away column still resolves — work_assignments.assignee_staff_id passed
the gate and was caught only by the provisioner failing at runtime.

commits.subject: fix(portfolio): make the doc-catalog check winnable, then gate on it
commits.body:
portfolio:sot:check could never pass, so nobody ran it, so DOC-CATALOG.md
drifted 71 files behind (299 indexed vs 370 on disk) before yesterday's
sweep surfaced it.

The cause was what the check compared. DOC-CATALOG.md embeds a "Live git
worktrees" table rendered from `git worktree list`, and the comparison
included it:

  - `main`'s HEAD sha advances with every commit, including the commit that
    carries the regenerated catalog — so regenerate-then-commit always left
    a file that was instantly stale by its own check;
  - CI has no sibling worktrees, so a runner would have failed against any
    locally-generated catalog, permanently. That is why this was never in
    ci.yml or verify.mjs.

Now the check normalizes out both the timestamp and the whole worktree
section, comparing the doc ROSTER only — the one claim the file makes that
is a property of the repo rather than of a machine or a moment. The
worktree table is still written; it just is not gated on.

Verified: sha-only drift passes; adding a doc fails; removing a doc fails;
the normalized form contains no worktree paths (so a runner and a laptop
agree), while retaining all 452 todo doc ids.

Wired into verify.mjs and ci.yml beside the schema-drift gate. Full
`npm run verify` green with it.

commits.subject: refactor(receiving): resolve the bench vocabulary from the station declaration
commits.body:
Completes the reconciliation the divergence guard was holding open. The bench
owned its own ordered step list and the Studio Procedure lens owned another;
both docblocks claimed to be "the operator-facing unbox procedure" and they
disagreed on granularity, on which steps existed, and on variant handling.

captureStepVocabulary keeps its name and signature — no call site moved — but
its body is now resolveProcedureSteps(getProcedure('unbox'), input, 'capture').
CAPTURE_STEPS and STEP_CLASSIFY are deleted; the variant rules (drop
packing_material on a pickup, serial-before-condition on a return, prepend
classify on unfound) exist once, declaratively, on the declaration.

This was safe to do unilaterally because the previous guard had already proved
it: it asserted both sides produced identical sequences across six carton
shapes BEFORE the swap, which makes this a behaviour-preserving refactor rather
than a rewrite. The module's own 18 tests pass unchanged.

Two type consequences, both deliberate. CaptureStepDef.key widens from the
closed CaptureStepKey union to string — this module no longer gets to close the
set — and CaptureStepKey, narrowed by isCaptureStepKey, becomes the separate
question of which keys it can GATE. The gate switch gains a safe fallback: an
unknown key renders NOT DONE rather than throwing, because a bench that crashes
mid-carton is worse than one showing an extra unchecked row.

The guard changed shape with the merge. Comparing two sequences is tautological
once both sides read one declaration, so it now pins the invariants that keep it
that way: the bench must declare no second ordered vocabulary, and every
declared capture step must have a gate (an ungated step would render permanently
unchecked and block the operator). Both proven to fail.

commits.subject: docs(motion): ratify the sidebar push snap under reduced motion
commits.body:
Closes the last open question from the Lane G verification: disabling the
sidebar nav column's width animation under prefers-reduced-motion is intended.

The reasoning is worth keeping because it is easy to mistake the snap for a
regression. The vestibular trigger is smooth continuous motion - the
in-between frames - so an instant state change does not trigger it. And there
is no crossfade equivalent of making room: the space either exists or it does
not. You can fade a slide; you cannot fade a reflow. This doc's own rule
sanctions the push animation partly because "the operator asked for it", which
is permission to animate, not a requirement to.

Also records the refinement that was considered and rejected, so it is not
rediscovered as a fresh idea: the inner aside is a plain element, so contents
could fade in while the box snaps, and opacity does still tween under the
floor. Rejected - it solves cognitive orientation rather than vestibular
safety, it makes the reduced path structurally different from the normal one
instead of a reduction of it, and it touches ContextPanelLayout and the photo
viewer drawer too. Revisit only on a real report of disorientation.

Two items stay open: CaptureStack / MobileFeed were never independently
measured, and there is no production-build hydration check.

commits.subject: feat(studio): reconcile the station procedure with the bench checklist
commits.body:
The Studio Procedure lens and the right-rail bench checklist were authored
independently, and both claimed IN THEIR OWN DOCBLOCKS to be "the
operator-facing unbox procedure" — while disagreeing. Studio declared 7 flat
steps; the bench declared 5 variant-aware ones. An operator being taught one
procedure at the bench while the owner reads a different one in Studio is
worse than either being wrong alone, because both look authoritative.

They were never in conflict — they were nested. The bench vocabulary is a
contiguous phase inside the full station procedure, so ProcedureStep gains one:

  intake  — how work reaches the bench (scan)
  capture — the per-carton acts; exactly what the checklist renders
  commit  — print / receive, which the terminal dock owns

resolveProcedureSteps(procedure, variant, phase?) becomes the single resolver:
Studio calls it with no phase, the bench with 'capture'. One declaration, two
slices, no second vocabulary. Variant rules are declarative and compose
(onlyWhen / omitWhen / moveBefore — filter first, then reorder), so an unfound
return resolves correctly instead of one rule clobbering the other.

The merge takes each side's better answer: the bench's three photo steps (they
map 1:1 onto photo-intent stages, and po_photos is a VERIFY step whose stage
the receive gate actually counts — a bench capture stamped there would void
the control), Studio's print + receive, and neither side's `queue`, because
picking from a rail is navigation rather than an act on the carton.

procedure-divergence.guard.test.ts pins the two in sync across six carton
shapes, including the combinations that co-occur. Proven to fail on a dropped
variant rule and on a mis-pointed reorder, both with the exact sequence diff.
It is a seam, not an end state: the follow-through is the bench importing the
resolver and captureStepVocabulary being deleted, written up for that lane in
docs/todo/procedure-reconciliation-MEMO.md.

Also removes a NUL byte that had crept into a template literal in
station-procedure-map.ts. It worked as a delimiter, so every test passed, but
it made git classify a .ts file as binary — no diff, no blame, no review.

stamps `set_by_staff_id` — a shared signal with no author is an anonymous
claim. Set from the multi-select bar (one bulk write for N rows) or the
inspector.

A flag is a NAMED TAG, never a raw swatch. Colour alone carries no meaning
across a handoff — two staffers will use yellow for two things inside a week —
so every flag pairs a tone with a word and a one-line hint, and the row carries
a dot + sr-only label so the tint is never the only carrier.

**Ops notes.** `order_notes` shipped in 2026-07-28 with no writers; these are
its first. Append-only with author + timestamp, replacing the legacy scalar
`orders.notes`, where the second person to touch a row overwrote the first and
nobody could tell who said either thing. The birth migration's scope boundary
holds: this is the internal ops trail, the customer conversation stays in
Entity Threads.

**Where things live** follows the action-plane law: the grid carries the
summary (tint, corner indicator), the record plane carries the reason and the
authors. Selection outranks the flag wash — the row being edited must look
picked, not tagged — but a flagged row keeps its tint under the pointer, since
a hover fill that erases it reads as "did I imagine that colour?".

Read path: the flag and note count are joined into the queue's row projection
as scalar subqueries on `o.id`, so they arrive with the row that renders them
rather than as an N+1 or a second request that repaints one frame late. That
had to be done in THREE places — this route's inline SQL, `ORDER_SERIALS_CTE`,
and `getActiveOrders` — because the outbound queue has three independent order
readers. Writes invalidate the 300s Redis queue cache; without that an
operator's flag silently does not appear for five minutes (caught in browser
verification, not in review).

`order_flags_flag_chk` — a discriminator whose two lists drift is exactly the

commits.subject: feat(grid): per-surface frozen identity pane; Orders spine = select · order · title
commits.body:
The frozen identity pane was a house-wide key list (GRID_IDENTITY_COLUMN_KEYS),
so six grid families each declared `LOCKED_KEYS = [...GRID_IDENTITY_COLUMN_KEYS]`
— identical only because no surface had yet needed a different pane. The first
one that did (Orders, adding the order id) would have had to fork a page-local
list or widen the constant onto five surfaces that have no order column.

Declare the pane on the column model instead (`frozen: true`) and derive the key
list with `gridFrozenKeys(columns)`. One declaration now drives all three
invariants — pinned-left, immovable under drag-reorder, never in-cell editable —
so freeze and the sticky-left offset math cannot drift apart.

Orders (/dashboard) freezes `select · order · title`: on a dispatch queue the
order is the container and the scan anchor (Shopify Admin / ShipStation pin it
first), with the product title as the heavy secondary anchor for the pick. Fact
columns rebalance to `ship-by · cond · qty · tracking`. Catalog / Receiving /
Incoming / Repair / Pickup keep `select · title` — Catalog has no order context,
and on Receiving/Incoming the PO is secondary to the item being scanned.

Promoting `order` into the pane retires its `hideKey` (a frozen column is
structural, so the Fields menu can never take the row's identity away). That is
the whole staff-prefs migration: `isGridColumnVisible` short-circuits on a
missing hideKey, so an existing `hidden: ['orderid']` delta goes inert.

Guard: grid-column-tier.guard.test.ts now derives the structural set from
`frozen` and asserts the pane is a contiguous leading prefix — the invariant the
offset math actually depends on.

per-staff SERVER pref, so a reorder test that died mid-run left its custom order
behind for every later test and run. A beforeEach clears it through the API; the

The QA sandbox already exists and solves this: a fixed QA_ORG_ID, deterministic

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(dashboard): restore the full bulk-bar reserve — pb-8 still covered rows
commits.body:
Reverts the pb-8 tuning from ba20f62f8 and adds the e2e guard that caught it.

That commit claimed the capsule cleared the last row by 2px at the default
pb-3, so a small reserve was enough. The measurement behind it came from an
in-app browser pane whose rects were distorted (the capsule's bottom read past
innerHeight). Playwright, desktop 1440x900, grid scrolled to its end:

  pb-3  (default) → scrollport 855 vs capsule 837 → -18px, ~half a row covered
  pb-8            → scrollport 835 vs capsule 832 →  -3px, still covering
  pb-20           → scrollport 787 vs capsule 832 → +45px

So the original overlap was real and pb-8 does not clear it.

pb-20 is sized to the capsule's own footprint (50px capsule + 16px viewport
gap = 68px) rather than to whatever the surrounding chrome happens to leave, so
the guarantee does not depend on the header, the KPI strip, or
WORKBENCH_BODY_COLUMN's padding staying put.

The spec asserts the grid's SCROLLPORT edge against the capsule top, not the
last row: the grid is virtualized, so the last row in the DOM belongs to the
render window and can sit below the fold (a first draft measuring it reported a
bogus -447px). Rows are clipped by the port, so the port edge is the lowest
pixel any row can occupy. Pending and Packed are both covered — they reach the
bounded host through independent prop chains.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(grid): make the self-scrolling LedgerGrid render, and its rows selectable
commits.body:
Station History was the first surface to mount a LedgerGrid that windows
against its OWN body instead of an ancestor scroll region, which surfaced
two defects that had been latent while the path sat dark behind a flag.

- The virtualizer took its scroll element from `bodyRef.current`, which is
  null on first render. Attaching a ref does not re-render, so nothing ever
  re-read it and the grid stayed permanently blank — no rows AND no empty
  state. It only appeared to work when an unrelated re-render happened to
  land after mount, which is what made it look intermittent. One post-mount
  render, gated to the self-scrolling case, lets getScrollElement() see the
  node. Ancestor-scroll consumers are untouched: their ref belongs to a
  parent that is already mounted when the grid first renders.

- Selection was unreachable. The gutter rendered an interactive checkbox
  only under `gridSkin`; every other selectMode consumer got an inert
  <span> that looked identical, while the row's own click handler only ever
  calls onRowClick. The control is now interactive whenever the caller
  supplies onToggleSelect — reaching for gridSkin instead would have
  dragged in Sheets-style in-cell editors, which do not belong on a
  scan-log surface.

Threading the virtualizer's absolute `rowIndex` through to the row also
fixes an a11y defect: without it the row claimed role="checkbox" inside a
role="table", i.e. a table with no rows at all. It is now role="row" with
aria-selected and a correct aria-rowindex.

Verified on /pack and /test?ship=history: 28 of 90 rows windowed, day bands
intact, select → "1 selected" → "2 selected", and row click still opens the
record without disturbing selection.

commits.body:

The capsule was not hiding rows. What was missing is any RULE keeping it from

the header, the KPI strip, or WORKBENCH_BODY_COLUMN's padding flips it negative.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(nav): the sidebar spine is a navigator, not a modal
commits.body:
Opening the nav painted `bg-scrim/40 backdrop-blur-[2px]` over the work surface
and locked body scroll, so on the dashboard it read as a modal takeover — and
the thing it dimmed was the order grid the operator was navigating *from*.

That is the call the right rail already made: modality is for surfaces that
genuinely block until dismissed, and a nav panel never does
(`source-of-truth.md` → Right-rail modality). The dashboard's right-edge
inspector is non-modal for exactly this reason, so a modal panel on the left of
the same surface was the inconsistency, not the standard.

The scrim becomes a transparent light-dismiss catcher: one click outside still
closes, which is the right contract for a panel you leave as soon as you have
chosen. Keeping the catcher rather than a document-level outside-click listener
also avoids racing the header toggle into close-then-reopen. Body scroll lock is
gone (`overflow: hidden` on body is the app shell's own baseline either way).

`role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` → `role="navigation"`. This never installed a
focus trap and must not: the station scan hotkey force-focuses a bar behind this
panel, which is why it closes on SCAN_FOCUS_REQUESTED_EVENT. `aria-modal`
without containment was a claim the DOM did not honor.

`data-sidebar-scrim` → `data-sidebar-dismiss`, and the spec that clicked it is
updated in the same change rather than left asserting a dead contract. Adds a
test pinning the non-modality so a scrim cannot come back silently.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: refactor(refresh): replace the global refresh broadcasts with typed domains
commits.body:
There was never an ['app-data'] query key. `app-refresh-data` was one global
broadcast with ten listeners spanning eight unrelated data domains, so every
emit — a Zoho sync, a photo move, a walk-in cart change — woke the repair list,
the packer logs, the replenish counts, the work-order calendar and the phone
history alike. `dashboard-refresh` was a second, overlapping copy of the same
idea.

Each site now names the domains its write actually touched, and only those
listeners run. Both broadcast names are deleted, along with the APP_REFRESH_DATA
and DASHBOARD_REFRESH constants.

The plan estimated 38 emit sites; the real total was ~70 across five mechanisms —
dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(…)), bare new Event(…), emitAppEvent(APP_REFRESH_DATA),
declarative event-name arrays consumed by useSidebarRail / useMobileFeed, and
useEventBridge handler maps. The last four were invisible to a grep for the
first. Both generic hooks gained a `refreshDomains` input beside their existing
`refreshEvents` / `windowEvents`, so per-feature events keep their own vocabulary.

`phone.history` turned out to be the packer-log feed under another name
(/api/packing-logs/history) and was collapsed into `packer.logs`.

Guarded: every domain needs at least one emitter AND one listener, no bundle may
cover every domain, and the retired names cannot come back. Verified in the
running app — the two riskiest mappings (walk-in sale → replenish, data wipe →
receiving.lines) each refetch their pane and leave the other seven domains alone.

Left in place deliberately, against the plan: receiving-package-updated carries a
payload used for optimistic setState patching (moving it to onSuccess would
REMOVE optimistic patching); receiving-scan-resolved is imperative scan-flow
signalling; sku-pairing-updated's listeners are hand-rolled fetch+useState with
no cache to invalidate; and receiving-clear-line is not redundant after the param
work — two of its three emitters are in-surface tab switches that keep recvId.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(receiving): isolate URL params by route ownership, not denylists
commits.body:
The Triage→Unbox leak was never routing. `applyModeTarget` copied the whole
query string to the destination and then hand-deleted whatever someone had
remembered to list — which is what MODE_SCOPED_PARAMS and the receiving half of
stripCrossSurfaceParams were. Every param added between the last edit and the
next bug was a silent leak.

Isolation is now (a) construct the target URL from a declared set instead of
copying, and (b) parse at the boundary against a per-route zod schema that drops
what the route never claimed. Route segments do NOT strip query params — Next.js
strips nothing — so they are not, and must never be described as, the mechanism.

Three denylists deleted: MODE_SCOPED_PARAMS, the receiving half of
stripCrossSurfaceParams, and clearReceivingHistoryUrlParams (dead once mode
switches construct). Vocabularies compose their existing SoT via paramRoundTrip
rather than copying the value lists.

Guards: param-ownership (one owner per param, plus a shrink-only ratchet on
undeclared reads), route-mode-registry, and an e2e that fails on the reported
bug — it did fail on the first run against the hook-only fix, which is how the
real culprit (the master nav's applyModeTarget) was found.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(dashboard): keep ?openOrderId= across a reload
commits.body:
Reloading the dashboard with a record open dropped it: the URL went from
`?unshipped=&openOrderId=5660` back to `?unshipped=`, the session snapshot was
cleared, and no panel mounted. That breaks the Workbench law that selection is
durable and URL-addressable.

Root cause (traced by instrumenting dispatchEvent + history.replaceState, not
inferred): the queue's stale-selection cleanup. On boot `?openOrderId=`
resolves and dispatches open-shipped-details BEFORE the queue's own rows have
arrived, so `visibleRecords.find(...)` misses. The effect read that as "the
record left the queue", called onCloseRecord -> close-shipped-details ->
clearSelectedOrder(true), which strips the param. A pure race; nothing was
wrong with the record.

The effect now distinguishes "rows are not here yet" from "the row left" — it
only closes a selection it has actually SEEN in this queue. Rows that are
deleted or filtered out under the operator still close exactly as before,
because those were seen first.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: feat(dashboard): non-modal, resizable order inspector
commits.body:
The details panel opened as a modal: aria-modal + body scroll lock + a
full-viewport scrim that dimmed and blurred the sidebar, KPI strip, lifecycle
tabs and every sibling row — exactly the context an operator needs while
editing one record. Reading and lightly editing a row mid-queue is a
non-modal job.

Modality is now a per-occupant contract on the right-rail store (`modal`,
default true so all ~11 occupants are unchanged). `RightRailHost` resolves it
for the scroll lock, the backdrop, and role/aria, replacing the hardcoded
`isAssistantDock` identity check. Only ShippedDetailsPanel opts out.

Note this also ends an a11y falsehood: the host has never installed a focus
trap, so `aria-modal="true"` was a claim the DOM did not honor. Non-modal
markup is the honest form — do not "fix" it by adding a trap.

Also in this commit, because they touch the same two files and cannot be
split without hunk surgery:

- Escape ownership. A capture-phase queue listener ran before every
  bubble-phase `useEscapeClose` and called stopPropagation(), so Escape inside
  an open condition popover or row menu closed the INSPECTOR and left the
  popover up. New overlay-stack store: the innermost open overlay owns
  Escape. AnchoredLayer registers, so every house Popover / menu / cell
  editor / Calendar participates; ambient owners stand down.
- Capture-phase Enter no longer hijacks a focused row (it only knew how to
  open records[0], so tabbing down and pressing Enter opened the wrong order).
- Drag-to-resize for non-modal occupants, min 360 / default 420, width
  persisted globally. The cap is derived, not taste: viewport minus the 360px
  sidebar and the grid's ~596px min content width.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: feat(a11y): absolute ARIA row numbering for the virtualized grid
commits.body:
Only a WINDOW of rows is ever in the DOM, so a screen reader previously had no
row structure at all and no way to know where it was: role="table" with no rows.
This adds the row half — role="row" + aria-rowindex on every row, aria-rowcount
on the table.

Indices are computed as if every fold were EXPANDED and never renumber. That is
the ARIA-recommended behaviour for collapsible rows, not a shortcut: keeping
indices stable while aria-rowcount holds the total is what stops a user losing
their place. The practical payoff is that nothing needs to know a fold's
expanded state, so `CollapsibleGroupRow`'s state stays where it is.

grid-row-index.ts owns the math (9 unit tests) and BOTH the count and the index
walk consume it, so aria-rowcount can never drift from the indices.

Two elements had to stop claiming an interactive role, because an element has
exactly one role and a table whose rows are `button`/`checkbox` has no rows:

  • CollapsibleGroupRow's summary → role="row"; aria-expanded is valid on row,
    which is how expandable rows are modelled, so the disclosure is unchanged.
  • OrdersQueueTableRow → role="row"; selection moves to aria-selected, and the
    real checkbox in the select cell is untouched, so nothing is lost.

Both are gated on being inside a table (`inTable`), so neither can become an
orphaned role if reused outside one. The virtualizer's positioning wrapper is
role="presentation" — a generic div between table and row breaks the required
context chain.

Wired end-to-end on the Orders/Pending path as the proving consumer. The other
five station grids are unaffected: rowIndex is optional, so they keep their
current behaviour until threaded.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(a11y): drop the orphaned role="row" from StationRowColumnHeader
commits.body:
This is a VISUAL column guide over legacy two-zone queue rows
(dashboardOrderRowShellClass), not a table header:

  • its own HeaderCells emit no role="columnheader", so the row owned no cells;
  • the rows it labels carry no table semantics at all;
  • StationListTable renders it standalone on the empty and non-virtualized
    paths, where it had no table/rowgroup ancestor — an orphaned role, and
    therefore spec-invalid (WAI-ARIA 1.2 §5.3.2 required context role).

Removing it is the honest change: AT users still get the header text, without a
claimed structure that isn't there. Restore the role only alongside real
columnheader cells AND a guaranteed table context.

E2E selectors are unaffected — they match [role="row"]:has([data-col="title"])
(the modern grid headers, which carry data-col) or the real <table> in settings.

Shrinks the guard allowlist from 7 to 6. No orphaned row/columnheader roles
remain anywhere in src.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: fix(a11y): give grid column headers valid ARIA context
commits.body:
The six LedgerGrid column headers asserted role="row" + role="columnheader"
inside a plain <div>. Both roles have a REQUIRED context role (WAI-ARIA 1.2
§5.3.2): row needs rowgroup/table/grid/treegrid, columnheader needs a row in a
table/grid. With no such ancestor the markup was spec-invalid partial table
semantics — worse than no roles, because it claims a structure that isn't there.

LedgerGrid now supplies the missing context: role="table" on the surface
(omitted while empty) and role="rowgroup" on the sticky header band.

role="table", NOT role="grid", is deliberate. ARIA grid is a composite widget;
asserting it obligates the full APG keyboard contract (roving tabindex,
arrow-key cell navigation, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End), which this shell does not
implement. table is the honest claim for tabular content whose cells may hold
widgets.

Also names every table: ariaLabel is REQUIRED on both composers every product
surface mounts (LedgerGridSurface, OrdersGridView) so a new grid cannot ship
anonymous. StationListTable takes it optional and falls back to bannerTitle —
it is wrapped by generic station adapters where a required prop would cascade.

Known remaining gap, deliberately not closed here: body rows still carry no
role="row"/aria-rowindex, so a virtualized list exposes no row structure. That
needs a decision on how folded groups map to ARIA and an absolute-index
contract through the virtualizer — see the follow-up brief, section 4.

Guard: grid-aria-roles.guard.test.ts pins the container/header half, fails if
the role is "upgraded" to grid without the keyboard model, and tracks the one
remaining orphan (StationRowColumnHeader on StationListTable's non-virtualized
path) on a shrink-only allowlist.
